newsitem.title: USA: WMX Technologies sees Q4 charge from deal.
newsitem.headline: WMX Technologies sees Q4 charge from deal.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said Wednesday that it expects it take a charge of about $88.0 million or $0.18 a share in the fourth quarter after its majority-owned Waste Management International Plc unit agreed to sell its stake in Wessex Water Plc.
WMX said sale of Wessex shares will cut its 1997 earnings by about $0.04 a share.
Earlier, Waste Management said it agreed to sell its 19.5 percent equity investment in Wessex.

Under terms of the proposed transaction, Waste Mangement will sell to Wessex about 87 percent of its shares in the United Kingdom-based utility. It will divest the remaining 13 percent of its investment in open market stock sales.
Total after-tax proceeds are expected to be about $259 million in cash.
The agreement is subject to approval by Wessex stockholders, but is expected to be completed in February 1997, it added.

"The agreement with Wessex represents another important step in our plans to simplify our organizational structure, narrow our scope of activities and enhance shareholder value," Phillip Rooney, WMX president, said in a statement. "The cash generated by Waste Management International from this transaction will be used to lower Waste Management International's debt and enable the unit to focus more capital on its core waste services business to increase shareholder value over the long term."
WMX said it expects to monetize additional assets, including non-core equity investments, real estate and underperforming core businesses.
